symptom: Engine overheating or high coolant temp warning
likely_cause: Radiator core packed with dust, low coolant, or a slipping fan belt
what_to_check: Park on level ground, dump body down, engine off and cooled for 30 minutes before opening anything. Check the coolant sight glass, blow out the radiator core from the back side, look for a loose or cracked belt.
call_tech_when: Coolant is low again after a top-off, there is coolant in the oil, or the warning comes back within an hour.

symptom: Payload readout looks wrong or too high
likely_cause: Payload system out of calibration, or a strut pressure sensor reading off
what_to_check: Park empty on level ground. Compare the readout empty against the last known tare weight. Check that all four struts sit at even height.
call_tech_when: The empty reading is more than 5 tons off, or one strut is visibly low. Strut work is tech only.

symptom: Retarder feels weak going downhill
likely_cause: Overheated retarder oil, or low brake cooling oil
what_to_check: Stop at the bottom of the grade, set the parking brake, idle at high idle to cool the oil. Check the brake cooling oil level once parked.
call_tech_when: The retarder temp gauge stays in the red, or the truck will not hold on the grade. Do not run it downhill loaded until a tech clears it.

symptom: Body will not raise or raises slowly
likely_cause: Low hydraulic oil, a cold system, or the hoist control in the wrong position
what_to_check: Park on level ground, nobody near the body. Check the hydraulic tank sight glass with the body down. Let the oil warm at idle for 10 minutes and try again.
call_tech_when: Oil level is fine and it still will not raise, or you see oil spraying. Never climb under a raised body without the body-up retaining pin in.

symptom: Low tire pressure warning
likely_cause: Slow leak, a cut tire, or a cold morning reading
what_to_check: Park, chock the wheels, stand clear of the tire sidewall. Walk around and look for cuts, bulges or a rim leak. Do not inflate a mining tire yourself.
call_tech_when: Any cut, bulge or a tire that is visibly low. Mining tires are a tech and tire crew job only.

symptom: Steering feels heavy or jerky
likely_cause: Low steering oil, or air in the system after a hose change
what_to_check: Park on level ground, install the steering frame lock before anyone walks between the frames. Check the hydraulic oil level and look for wet hoses at the hitch.
call_tech_when: Oil level is fine and steering is still heavy, or any hose at the hitch is leaking.

symptom: Truck will not shift out of first gear
likely_cause: Transmission in limp mode from a fault code, or low transmission oil
what_to_check: Park, engine off for one minute, then restart to clear a soft fault. Check the transmission oil with the engine idling and warm.
call_tech_when: The fault code comes back after a restart. Read the code off the display for the tech.

symptom: Grinding or clunking when it swings
likely_cause: Low swing gear oil, worn swing bearing, or loose swing bearing bolts
what_to_check: Bucket on the ground, engine off, hydraulic lock lever up. Check the swing drive oil level and the swing bearing grease. Listen for where the noise is coming from at slow swing.
call_tech_when: Metal in the swing drive oil, the noise gets worse, or there is play in the upper when you rock it. Stop swinging under load until a tech looks.

symptom: Hydraulics slow or weak across all functions
likely_cause: Low hydraulic oil, plugged return filter, or the machine in an eco or fine-swing mode
what_to_check: Bucket on the ground, engine off, lock lever up. Check the hydraulic sight glass, then check the power mode on the monitor is set to standard or high.
call_tech_when: Oil is full, mode is right, and it is still slow, or the hydraulic temp is high.

symptom: Hydraulic oil leaking at a cylinder or hose
likely_cause: A blown hose, a loose fitting, or a cylinder seal
what_to_check: Lower the bucket to the ground and shut down. Never run a hand along a hose to find a leak: pressurized oil can inject through skin. Look from a distance and note where it is wet.
call_tech_when: Any leak while running, a spraying hose, or oil on the ground that keeps spreading. Shut it down and call a tech.

symptom: Tracks keep coming off or one track is loose
likely_cause: Track tension too loose, or a worn idler
what_to_check: Park on level ground, bucket down, lock lever up. Measure the track sag at the middle of the top run compared with the operator manual.
call_tech_when: The track comes off again after tensioning, or the grease fitting will not hold tension. Never loosen the track adjuster yourself: it is under high pressure.

symptom: Machine travels crooked
likely_cause: One travel motor weak, or a track packed with mud
what_to_check: Park, bucket down. Clean out the tracks and sprockets, then test travel on flat ground at slow speed.
call_tech_when: It still pulls to one side on clean tracks. That is a travel motor or valve, tech only.

symptom: Brakes feel soft or the brake warning comes on
likely_cause: Low brake oil, or low accumulator charge
what_to_check: Stop, set the parking brake, lower the bucket flat on the ground. Check the brake oil level. Do not move the loader if the brake warning stays on.
call_tech_when: The warning stays on after the engine runs a few minutes. The machine stays parked until a tech clears it.

symptom: Bucket drifts down when parked
likely_cause: A leaking lift cylinder seal or a control valve leaking by
what_to_check: Lower the bucket flat on the ground any time you leave the seat. Mark the cylinder rod and see how far it drifts in 10 minutes with the engine off and the bucket raised a little, nobody under it.
call_tech_when: It drifts more than an inch in 10 minutes. Never work under a raised bucket.

symptom: Engine smoking black under load
likely_cause: Plugged air filter or a boost leak
what_to_check: Bucket down, engine off. Check the air filter restriction indicator and look over the intake hoses for a loose clamp.
call_tech_when: The filter is clean and it still smokes, or you hear a whistle from the turbo.

symptom: Blade or ripper will not lift
likely_cause: Low hydraulic oil, or the implement lockout switch is on
what_to_check: Blade and ripper on the ground, engine off. Check the hydraulic sight glass and that the implement lockout on the console is off.
call_tech_when: Oil and the lockout are fine and it still will not lift.

symptom: Squealing or popping from the undercarriage
likely_cause: Dry track pins, a cracked roller, or packed material
what_to_check: Park on level ground, blade and ripper down. Walk the undercarriage and look for a roller that is not turning or material packed in the frame.
call_tech_when: A roller is not turning, there is a crack, or the noise keeps up after cleaning.

symptom: Engine derates or loses power
likely_cause: Fuel filter plugged, water in the fuel, or a DEF or aftertreatment warning
what_to_check: Blade down, park. Drain the water separator. Read the warning on the display: a DEF warning means check the DEF level.
call_tech_when: Power does not come back after the water is drained and DEF is full, or an aftertreatment fault shows.

symptom: Moldboard will not hold its angle
likely_cause: Air in the circle drive, or a worn circle shear pin
what_to_check: Park, moldboard on the ground, engine off. Look at the circle drive for leaks and check for a sheared pin.
call_tech_when: The pin is sheared or the circle slips again after a restart.

symptom: Joystick controls not responding
likely_cause: A fault code locking out implements, or the implement lockout is on
what_to_check: Park, set the parking brake. Check that the implement lockout is off, then cycle the key to clear a soft fault.
call_tech_when: The controls stay dead after a restart. Read the code off the display for the tech.

symptom: Spray heads will not come on
likely_cause: Water pump not engaged, a plugged strainer, or an empty tank
what_to_check: Park, set the parking brake, pump off. Check the tank level and pull and clean the suction strainer.
call_tech_when: The pump runs and the strainer is clean but nothing sprays, or the pump makes noise.

symptom: Water cannon will not aim
likely_cause: Cannon joystick fault, or low hydraulic oil on the cannon circuit
what_to_check: Park, pump off. Check the hydraulic oil level and that the cannon control is switched on in the cab.
call_tech_when: Oil is fine and the cannon still will not move.

symptom: Compressor overheating on long holes
likely_cause: Dirty compressor cooler, or the ambient air too hot for the duty cycle
what_to_check: Stop drilling, pull the steel, let the compressor idle down. Shut down and clean the cooler core once it is cool.
call_tech_when: It overheats again on a clean cooler, or the oil level drops. Compressor work is tech only.

symptom: Generator shuts down with a fault
likely_cause: Low fuel, low coolant, or an overload trip
what_to_check: Turn off the load at the breaker first. Check fuel and coolant. Read the fault code on the control panel before resetting.
call_tech_when: It trips again under the same load, or the fault code is not a fuel or overload code. Never open the panel: tech only.

symptom: Lights will not come on
likely_cause: Low fuel on the tower engine, a tripped breaker, or the timer set wrong
what_to_check: Mast down before you touch anything on the tower. Check fuel, the breaker on the panel, and the timer setting.
call_tech_when: The engine runs, breakers are on, and still no lights.

symptom: Warning light or fault code you do not recognize
likely_cause: Many possible causes
what_to_check: Park in a safe spot, lower all implements to the ground, set the parking brake, engine off. Write down the exact code or light from the display.
call_tech_when: Any red warning or stop light. Do not run the machine until a tech clears it.
